facts.text: Vacaville was founded in 1851 and named after Juan Manuel Vaca, a landowner who sold part of his Rancho Los Putos to William McDaniel.
The Buck family’s legacy lives on in Buck Avenue, a tree‑lined boulevard that once housed the original Vacaville Museum opened in 1984 after Eva Buck’s donation.
The Nut Tree, a 1920s roadside fruit stand, once featured a half‑mile railroad with tunnels and bridges, and a modern version still operates inside Nut Tree Plaza.
Every December, downtown Vacaville hosts a Festival of Trees where a 50‑foot tree lights up, the Jepson Band plays, and horse‑drawn carriages glide across the ice rink.
Vacaville’s Peña Adobe Historical Area preserves the 19th‑century Peña Adobe home and the Mowers‑Goheen Museum, showcasing early pioneer life.
